chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn Abī al-Khaṭṭāb, from al-Ḥakam ibn Miskīn, from Muḥammad ibn Marwān, who said:

Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “There may come upon a man sixty or seventy years in which Allah has not accepted any salat (prayer) from him.” I said: “And how is that?” He said: “Because he washes what Allah has commanded to be wiped.”

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Imam Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام, the speaker of the hadith
key_terms.أَمَرَ اللَّهُ: Allah commanded, indicating the binding divine instruction
key_terms.صَلَاةً: salat (prayer), whose acceptance depends on proper ritual preparation
key_terms.مَسْحِهِ: wiping it, the act Allah commanded in place of washing
key_terms.يَغْسِلُ: he washes, referring here to an incorrect act in wudu (ablution)

ai.seo_question: Why might Allah not accept a person’s salat (prayer) for many years بسبب an incorrect wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith emphasizes the legal importance of performing wudu (ablution) exactly as Allah has commanded. It warns that persistent error in washing a limb that is to be wiped can invalidate the acceptance of salat (prayer) over many years. The narration highlights precision in ritual purity as a necessary condition for valid worship.
